nodes.title: Canonical Higgs sheaves and stability
nodes.statement: A canonical Higgs sheaf is (F,θ:F→F⊗Ω_X), with morphisms commuting with θ. For rank r>0 its slope is d/r. It is semistable if every nonzero proper θ-invariant coherent subsheaf W has μ(W)≤μ(F), and stable if all such inequalities are strict, assigning torsion slope +∞. Saturated subsheaves suffice for bundles. Positive-rank semistable Higgs sheaves are bundles. This category has HN filtrations by Higgs subsheaves; its Ext groups are hypercohomology of the two-term Hom complex and need not vanish in degree 2. On locally free objects this reuses ET.2b/hitchin-moduli-stack for G=GL_r and D=Ω_X. Also define the full positive subcategory A_K^+ by μ_min(F)≥0, with the exact structure induced from coherent Higgs sheaves. Relative (semi)stability tests invariant subobjects belonging to A_K^+ (the quotient is then positive). It is not defined by intersecting the usual semistable locus with A_K^+. For g≥1 and d>binom(r,2)(2g−2), the relative and usual semistable moduli agree; outside that range no equality is asserted.
proofSteps: Reuse the canonical GL_r bundle Higgs carrier from ET.2b; extend its interface to coherent sheaves and the HN-nonnegative exact subcategory without defining another bundle carrier.
Show the torsion subsheaf is invariant; it destabilizes every positive-rank object with torsion.
Establish bounded maximal Higgs slopes and the HN induction; compute the two-term deformation complex with the supplier coherent cohomology.

For a semistable Higgs bundle of rank s, consecutive underlying HN slopes differ by at most 2g−2. The binomial degree bound forces positivity; applying the same bound to a semistable destabilizer proves the converse comparison of the two stability conditions (MS14 Corollary 3.3).
acceptance: Do not require every underlying bundle to be semistable.
The Higgs category is not asserted hereditary.

nodes.statement: For g≥1, r>0, gcd(r,d)=1 put l=2g−2 and B=d/r−(r−1)l. Choose the least integer d_1≥0 with d_1>2g−1−B and (1−g+d_1)r+d>0. Set l_1=(1−g+d_1)r+d. A positive-rank semistable destabilizer has rank s≤r and slope>d/r, hence the same bound B. Every torsion sheaf is strongly generated by any line: its H¹ vanishes and its evaluation is surjective.

Use the requested degree-only criterion μ_min(F)+d_i>2g−1 for strong generation. For a nonzero kernel K of L1^{l1}↠F, let t=rk K=l1−r. Since μ_max(K)≤−d1 and deg K=−l1d1−d, μ_min(K)≥deg K−(t−1)μ_max(K)≥−d−(r+1)d1. If t=0, K is the zero bundle and is strongly generated.

The bound on d2 is strictly stronger than the generation threshold for these kernels and for L1. The congruence gives l2≡r mod l1, while l1≡d mod r, so gcd(l1,l2)=1.
